title: phplyr backends and dplyr
label: Backends and dplyr
description: Three pipelines on a generated sales table of 100,000 and 1,000,000 rows, joined to a 100-row stores table. A filters, joins, summarises by two keys, and ranks within groups. B computes lag(), cumsum(), and a share of the group total over every row. C is A with a PHP closure in filter(), so it has no dplyr version. The PHP backends run the same phplyr code.

columns.sales: id, store (100 values), product (1,000), day (1-365), units (about 2% NA, 5% zero), price

check.php_backends: Every backend returned the same rows as DataFrame, compared as sorted rows with floats to 9 significant digits.
check.dplyr: dplyr's row counts and numeric column sums matched DataFrame's within 1e-9 relative.

implementations.SQLite: phplyr on phibble's SqlTable, SQLite 3.45.1 through PDO

method: PHP: the pipeline through collect(), with the tables already loaded. dplyr: the pipeline on a tibble already in memory. Reading and generating the data are not timed.
time_spent_in: the PHP process for DataFrame, PolarsTable, and SQLite, which run inside it; the R process for dplyr.

A: filter, join, summarise, and rank (10.DataFrame:
fn (Table $s, Table $st) => $s
    |> filter(col('units')->gt(0))
    |> left_join($st, by: 'store')
    |> group_by('region', 'product')
    |> summarise(n: n(), revenue: sum(col('units')->mul(col('price'))), avg_price: mean('price'))
    |> group_by('region')
    |> mutate(rank: min_rank(desc('revenue')))
    |> filter(col('rank')->le(10))
    |> arrange('region', 'rank')

B: grouped windows over every row (100,0.DataFrame:
fn (Table $s, Table $st) => $s
    |> group_by('store')
    |> mutate(prev: lag('units', orderBy: 'day'), running: cumsum('units'), share: col('units')->div(sum('units', naRm: true)))
